outcome_summary: Died while starving after repeated preparation and combat stalls
improvements: When required loot needs potion preparation already underway, the bot now continues its existing stash-and-return routine instead of starting another approach to the same loot.
incoming_learnings: When required loot depends on potion preparation already in progress, let the existing stash workflow advance before selecting another test approach. Keep potion identities unknown until publicly established, verify every drop and pickup, and retain the upgrade obligation until collection is observed.

review.review: The Mage died while starving after prolonged preparation and combat stalls. The final accepted wait at decision 4562 (lines 13161-13162) changes health from 1 to 0; a particular enemy killer is not established. An earlier mandatory-pool block at decision 3021 already caused fallback while hungry. A separate, reproducible preparation defect then repeatedly reopened entrance 732 after returning to dry bank 731 (decisions 3176-3187), eventually reaching the navigation-loop guard at decision 3204. Ordinary doors close on departure, but the played helper required another opening each time. Source inspection and an offline helper reconstruction from public geometry and inventory bookkeeping reproduce the earlier opening and return inputs. The proposed correction first changes decision 3178 to a guarded unknown-potion test; investigation stops there, without using later observations as its continuation. A new deterministic regression fails on original policy copies with the expected assertion and passes on the candidate. All 1,593 Python tests pass, with four skips. This establishes a receipt repair, not chest retrieval, potion identity, or improved survival. Other backlog cases remain unresolved.
review.learnings: An ordinary door closing behind the hero does not erase an observed successful scouting arrival. Retain that receipt, but replan the full protected round trip and verify the actual potion effect before entering danger. Do not treat preparation as collection or infer unknown potion identities.

recommendations.summary: Establish an admitted dry-engagement or charge-preservation alternative before changing Goo combat priorities.
evidence: Decision 1453, selection line 4015: wakes Goo on water with full health and six staff charges.
Decisions 1460–1464, lines 4029–4046: melee trades on water consume health while four charges remain.
Decisions 1469–1470, lines 4055–4062: health falls from 27 to 12 during further melee trades.
Decision 1481, line 4087: exhausted-magic withdrawal starts; decision 1493, line 4136: fallback retreat follows.
recommendations.reason: Complete source explains the selection but establishes no discrete implementation defect or validated safe replacement. At decision 1460 the observed adjacent dry steps do not provide the separating landing required by the existing lure rule. A repair needs an admitted multi-turn dry-engagement route or a public-input-validated attack/resource alternative preserving warning escape and health/hunger budgets. Arbitrarily preferring magic, extending preparation, or guessing potion identities is not sufficient evidence.

recommendations.reason: No safe focused replacement is established. The public geometry admits protected chest trips from some approaches, but not an unknown-drink bank satisfying the existing dry-surroundings gates; no carried known invisibility or safe identification supply is recorded at the block. A repair needs evidence of an admissible identification/test-and-inventory-protection route, or additional public observations establishing one. Merely adding a pool meal would not resolve the recorded post-meal failure, and speculative movement or weakened hazard checks is not justified.
